meta.name: Validation gates — a strategy must pass every gate before it may be called skilful, ranked, or rewarded
meta.frozenRule: These thresholds are frozen on the date above, before any strategy result was computed. Changing a threshold requires a new version number and a new freeze date; the change is logged in the Gate change log below. A threshold changed after results were seen is evidence the result was fitted.
meta.passRule: All gates must pass. A gate that cannot be evaluated yet returns 'not evaluable' — never 'pass'.
meta.why: The purpose of a gate is to say no. A gate that always passes is decoration.

gates.name: Provenance
gates.question: Does every input value come from a named official source, with a URL and a retrieval time?
gates.passCondition: 100% of input rows carry sourceUrl + retrievedUTC, and the URL is on the approved official-domain list.
gates.failCondition: Any row with no source, an unofficial host, or an invented value.

gates.name: Correlation honesty
gates.question: Are dependent outcomes treated as dependent?
gates.passCondition: No parlay or combo price is published from a product of independent leg probabilities. Every combination shows the empirical joint probability, the independence product, and the signed difference, with n and an interval.
gates.failCondition: Any published combo price that silently assumes independence.
gates.evaluatedBy: nfl/tools/verify_nfl.py (scans for independence products presented as prices)

gates.name: Skill vs luck
gates.question: Could this result have arisen from a coin that knows nothing?
gates.passCondition: Observed proper score beats the shuffled-outcome distribution at p < 0.05, AND the strategy has at least the minimum settled sample, AND its calibration error is within tolerance.
gates.failCondition: p >= 0.05, or sample below minimum, or calibration error above tolerance.
gates.note: The minimum sample of 100 is a policy default (Q03), not a fact. It is set high deliberately: with 20 settled bets a 60% win rate is indistinguishable from luck.

gates.name: Calibration
gates.question: When the model says 60%, does it happen 60% of the time?
gates.passCondition: Expected calibration error (ECE) over deciles <= 0.07 and no decile off by more than 0.15 with n>=20 in that decile.
gates.failCondition: ECE above tolerance, or a badly miscalibrated decile.

gates.name: Uncertainty
gates.question: Is the uncertainty printed next to the estimate?
gates.passCondition: Every published estimate carries n and a 90% interval; estimates with n below the suppression floor are withheld entirely.
gates.failCondition: A point estimate with no n, or an estimate published below the floor.

gates.name: Honesty labelling
gates.question: Is every non-official number labelled as a model output?
gates.passCondition: Every computed value carries MODEL or ESTIMATE; every unpublishable value is blank with an UNVERIFIED badge; no page claims a verified value that has no official source.
gates.failCondition: A computed number presented as a fact, or a blank cell with no badge.

gates.name: Multiple testing
gates.question: If 40 strategies were tried, is the winner still surprising?
gates.passCondition: Benjamini–Hochberg style false-discovery control across all strategies tested in the same cycle, at q = 0.10, applied to the G3 p-values.
gates.failCondition: A strategy promoted on a p-value that does not survive the false-discovery correction.
gates.note: This is the gate that removes 'we tried everything until something worked'. It raises the bar as the number of tested strategies grows.

gates.name: Governance
gates.question: Who decided, when, and on what evidence?
gates.passCondition: Every promotion, demotion and reward decision names a reviewer, a date, and a reason; the gate version that applied is printed alongside.
gates.failCondition: An accepted strategy with no named reviewer.

gates.name: Point-in-time integrity
gates.question: Was the information used actually available at the moment the bet would have been made?
gates.passCondition: Every input carries a publication time; nothing published after the decision cutoff may be used. Lineup news after the cutoff is excluded.
gates.failCondition: Any input whose publication time is after the cutoff, or any input with no publication time.
gates.note: The injury report is published during the week; the final game-status update is published 90 minutes before kickoff per NFL rules. Anything inside the last hour cannot be used.
gates.evaluatedBy: requires a stored publication timestamp per input (not yet available for all sources — Q13)
